versionen_support.v1: Atheros ar71xx platform. Also sold as WNDR37AV-100PES, WNDR3700-100PES
versionen_support.v2: Atheros ar71xx platform. Box side panel lists WNDR3700v2, also sold as WNDRMAC-100PES, WNDR3700-100PRS
versionen_support.v3: Broadcom SoC, same hardware as WNDR4000. 5 GHz wireless did not work on older builds, and probably still does not.
versionen_support.v4: Atheros platform like v1 and v2, NAND flash, same PCB as WNDR4300, but only 2T2R. May be labeled as WNDR3700-100PES on the packaging's side panel (like some v1 models).
versionen_support.v5: MediaTek SoC. Supported as of r49247. This, too, may be labeled WNDR3700-100PES on the packaging.
versionen_support.WNDR37AV: Netgear has sold a number of WNDR3700v2 units in boxes marked WNDR37AV. The hardware is exactly identical to version 2

info_tabelle_v1.Flash-Chip: v1: Spansion S25FL064P (FL064PIF) or Macronix MX25L6405DMI-12G

openwrt_wiki.versionserkennung: The v2 revision may not be shown on the router bottom label. V1 and v2 seem to share the same EAN barcodes. If you have the original box, look under "Package Contents" it will say "N600 Wireless Dual Band Gigabit Router (WNDR3700v2)" for version 2, and just "WNDR3700" for version 1. The Netgear firmware GUI shows the "Hardware Version" in the "Maintenance" section under "Router Status". Also, the OEM version version for v1 is 1.0.4.x and higher, while v2 is 1.0.1.x or less.
openwrt_wiki.chargenproblem_v1: There are rumours that a certain batch of version 1 routers have problems with the 2,4 GHz radio suddenly dying. These came in boxes marked as -01R14 or -01R15 on the barcode label. It is also said that -01R21 or -02R01 are expected to be working o.k. Board version 4 is said to be reliable.
openwrt_wiki.hinweis_5g: 5G radio many not be detected after new install. It appeared after a power cycle. (beobachtet an v4)
openwrt_wiki.firmware_hinweis_v1: The v1 North America factory image is not getting listed: openwrt-18.06.2-ar71xx-generic-wndr3700-squashfs-factory-NA.img
openwrt_wiki.installation_oem_gui: stock WNDR3700 GUI, factory.img; Non North American users will get a warning regarding that OpenWrt identifies itself as NA, ignore
openwrt_wiki.installation_tftp: static 192.168.1.x; hold 'System Restore' button on the underside while powering on until power led steadily blinks green; TFTP .img to 192.168.1.1; router will not accept the firmware when the filename is too long, firmware.img should work; flashing takes a few minutes
openwrt_wiki.installation_seriell: U-Boot unterbrechen, ggf. "protect off all", fsload, TFTP 192.168.1.1; v1: openwrt-ar71xx-generic-wndr3700-squashfs-factory.img
openwrt_wiki.nmrpflash: auf 3700v2 genannt; nach Meldung noch ca. 1 min warten (Flash wird ~30 s weiter beschrieben)
openwrt_wiki.recovery: power on, press and hold RESET as soon as switch LEDs light up, until power LED flashes orange then green, release, TFTP to 192.168.1.1; bei kaputtem Image geht der Router selbst in TFTP-Recovery (Power-LED blinkt langsam)
openwrt_wiki.failsafe: when the power LED changes from steady orange to blinking green, press any button (WPS, Wifi or reset) within two seconds
openwrt_wiki.switch_hinweis: Firmware 24.10.3 (and earlier) use swconfig for this device, not DSA; Problem mit internem Switch (Traffic zu WLAN-Client), Workaround 'learning and aging' abschalten, https://dev.openwrt.org/ticket/13612
openwrt_wiki.gehaeuse_oeffnen: Torx (T-8); two screws easily visible on the bottom of the case; four more screws under the rubber feet (not glued, tethered)
openwrt_wiki.seriell: Internal J1 4-pin connector. 3.3V serial port voltage. Do not connect the 3.3V line. 115200 8N1, no flow control. WNDR3700v1: Pin1 3.3V, Pin2 TX, Pin3 RX, Pin4 GND
openwrt_wiki.seriell_kabel: ribbon cable to the header, IDC socket slides onto the board without soldering; cable can be snaked out between the 4-port LAN jack and the WAN jack
openwrt_wiki.jtag: Internal J3 connector, 14-pin: 1 TRST, 3 TDI, 5 TDO, 7 TMS, 9 TCK, 11 RST, 13 NC, 2-10 GND, 12 NC, 14 3.3VDC
openwrt_wiki.ram_mod: RAM-Aufrüstung mit 2x Samsung K4H511638D-UCCC (DDR400 32Mx16, TSOP-II 66pin) beschrieben
openwrt_wiki.antennen_mod: Revision 1: U.FL-Anschlüsse PJ2/PJ4 (5 GHz) und PJ5/PJ6 (2.4 GHz) nutzbar, Lötbrücken AS6/AS8/AS10, RP-SMA-Buchsen ins Gehäuse; Revision 2 nur U.FL für 5 GHz

openwrt_git_antennen.titel: ath79: wndr3700 series: fix wifi range & throughput
openwrt_git_antennen.text: Based on the PCB pictures, the WNDR3700(v1) really had eight independent antennae. Four antennae for each radio and all of those were printed on the circut board. The WNDR3700v2 and later have just six antennae ... remaining two are special 5GHz Rayspan Patch Antennae. 2.4 GHz uses fixed antenna group 1, 5 GHz (v1) fixed antenna group 2 via GPIO demultiplexer; Fixes FS#3088

lauf.notiz: Gluon-Image netgear-wndr3700 = OpenWrt netgear_wndr3700 = Hardware v1 (v2 hat eigenes Image). Ausgewertet: ToH-Dump + Live-hwdata, OpenWrt-Wiki (Seite für v1-v5), OpenWrt-Commits (ar71xx 2009, ath79 2018, Antennen-Fix 2020), DTS/dtsi/generic.mk, Gluon-Target und Commit 523dead (v2022.1), DeviWiki (= WikiDevi-Spiegel), FCC PY308300092: Etikett-Zeichnung, Handbücher 2009/2011, Außen- und Innenfotos. Werkstatt: nur WNDR3700 v4 in sackgasse-2021.md erwähnt, nichts zu v1. Strom 12 V 2.5 A Hohlstecker Mitte plus (Maß offen), innen, Tisch/Standfuß/Wand per Schlüssellöcher, 5x Gigabit, 1x USB 2.0, 2x2 b/g/n + 2x2 a/n mit 8 internen Leiterplattenantennen, 8 MB NOR/64 MB RAM, serielle Stiftleiste J1 115200 3.3 V, kein Lüfter. openwrt.org verlangt TLS-Kurve P-256 (nur --curves X25519 gibt handshake failure), daher dort --curves X25519:P-256.
